What Is Alien: Earth?

Alien: Earth is the latest sci-fi series crafted by Noah Hawley, serving as an ambitious prequel to the original Alien film franchise.

Premiering Tuesday, August 12, it centers on Wendy (Sydney Chandler), the first human-alien hybrid, who leads a high-stakes investigation into the crash site of a mysterious spaceship.

Joining Chandler are notable actors—Timothy Olyphant, Alex Lawther, Samuel Blenkin, Essie Davis, and a talented ensemble cast—taking the Alien mythology into bold new territory.

How to Watch Alien: Earth Without a Cable Subscription

Alien: Earth airs on FX and is available to stream via Hulu starting August 12 at 5 p.m. PT / 8 p.m. ET, with new episodes premiering weekly through September 23. Several streaming services make it accessible without traditional cable:

Hulu + Live TV: Offers FX live, plus Hulu, Disney+, and ESPN+; new users can claim a 3-day free trial.

FuboTV: Carries FX and offers a free 7-day trial — perfect for watching Alien: Earth early.

Sling and DirecTV Stream: Also include FX in their packages; some offer trial periods or promotional pricing.

How Alien: Earth Fits into the Alien & Predator Canon

Positioning itself as a prequel to the iconic Alien film series, Alien: Earth explores the origins of the Alien/human hybrid concept through Wendy’s journey.

While not directly featuring Predator elements, this expansion enriches the broader shared universe, offering fresh insight into the cosmic horror foundation that fans cherish. It fills narrative gaps and expands the Alien timeline in a compelling way.
